Posted December 1, 2005
(MarijuanaNews note: Today is World AIDS Day, and there will be many noble sounding speeches, but no one will mention the one thing that could help millions of the poorest people with AIDS around the world medical cannabis. Even in advanced countries, such a Canada, governments are failing to provide realistic access to medical cannabis.
See
World AIDS Day: More Proof That the Suppression Of Medical Cannabis Indeed Cannabis Prohibition Itself Is Mass Murder. Analysis by Richard Cowan

Consequently, the Free Canadian Party is doing something with the potential to help Canadians with serious medical problems get quality cannabis at reasonable prices. Their new website is an interesting experiment in community organization and self-defense for the most vulnerable members of society, sick, dying and disabled people whose medicine remains illegal.)

For Immediate release:
December 1, 2005

As a result of Health Canada's continuing failure to obey court orders to provide sick, dying, and disabled Canadians with realistic access to safe and affordable medical grade cannabis, the Free Canadian Party is launching a website to meet that need. (The site is online now, but the service will not be operating until Saturday.)
See
Philippe Lucas Analysis of the Consequences of Health Canada's Failure to Obey the Ontario Court's Ruling On Medical Cannabis. Is Cannabis Legal in Canada?

The FCP and its website, freecanadianparty.org, will not be directly involved in the buying and selling of cannabis. It is a purely informational service that will give patients a way to address their medical needs easily, safely and economically.

Based on a survey published in 2000 in the Canadian Medical Association Journal, it is estimated that two percent of Canadians, over 600,000 people, were using cannabis medically. It is likely that there are far more Canadians using cannabis medically today, as a result of a growing recognition of its therapeutic and palliative value.
See
There Are Already Almost 600,000 Canadian Medical Marijuana Users, But Health Canada Has Only Approved 40 2 Articles With Interesting Lesson In Spin.

Nonetheless, Health Canada has only been willing or able to provide legal exemptions to roughly 1,000 of those in need. Even with such a legal exemption, most patients must still rely upon either the black market to get their medicine, or grow their own. For many patients, neither option is feasible. Moreover, Health Canada's own supply of medical cannabis has been widely criticized by patients as being both overpriced and disappointing in its quality.
See
Hypocrisy and Democracy: Raid on Medical Cannabis Research Facility Critical of Health Canada's Schwag Challenges Canada's Values. What Will The Politicians Say?

Unfortunately, because of the recalcitrance of the Canadian medical establishment in recognizing the value of cannabis to many of their patients, it is not always possible for patients to substantiate their need for medical conditions.

Consequently, in keeping with the Ontario court ruling in the Parker case, all that will be required for FCP members will be a letter of diagnosis from a Canadian doctor.
See
Canadian Court Says Lack of Provision for Medical Marijuana Violates Fundamental Rights; Gives Parliament 12 Months to Fix Prohibition Laws -- Or Marijuana Possession Is Legal in Largest Province.

The Free Canadian Party hopes that its new website will serve as a vehicle for patients, both with and without legal exemptions, to connect with growers who can provide them with medical quality cannabis. Following the well-established models of other online communities, such as Ebay, the FCP hopes that this new service will allow qualified suppliers to develop their reputations as reliable sources, while competing side by side with other providers to keep prices low.

The patients can then order their medicine by mail, and not have to leave the comfort and safety of their homes. For people with serious health problems, this can make the difference between a tolerable life and a miserable death. Also, most people with serious health problems have very limited incomes and they should be able to get the best medicine at the best prices by avoiding the black market, or even buyers clubs with their overhead. The FCP believes that this new approach meets the true meaning of harm reduction.

In the end this is really about the patients. They deserve to feel a little joy and healing in their otherwise painful lives, especially at this time of the year.

For more info, contact: steve@freecanadianparty.org
